title: Conditional legislation and executive fact-finding
summary: Conditional legislation makes a legal consequence chosen by Congress depend on a factual condition that an executive official determines.
notes:
Begin by identifying the consequence Congress fixed, the condition that activates it, and the discretion involved in determining that condition. Brig Aurora accepts revival of trade restrictions when the President proclaims the relevant foreign-policy event. Field applies the idea to reciprocal trade treatment and tariffs that Congress itself specified.

The difficult question is whether the apparent condition embeds an unresolved policy choice. Field’s separate opinion treats judgments of unreasonable foreign treatment and the just duration of a suspension as legislative, while the majority treats them as administration. The category supplies an analytical distinction; the label fact-finding does not resolve how much discretion the statute actually grants.
